title: Pass by value, reference and const reference
summary: What each parameter style copies, why by-value vectors in recursion are a hidden O(n²), and lambdas capturing by reference.

sections.title: The three styles
sections.body:
✍️ `void f(vector<int> a)` — copies a. Changes inside f do not affect the caller. Costs O(n) per call.
✍️ `void f(vector<int>& a)` — no copy. Changes affect the caller.
✍️ `void f(const vector<int>& a)` — no copy, read-only. Default choice for inputs.

sections.title: In recursion and backtracking
sections.body:
✍️ Pass the input as `const&`, and the "current path" as `&` with push/pop (choose → recurse → undo). See [[bt-pick-or-skip#undo]].
✍️ Passing `path` by value is correct but copies it on every call; acceptable for tiny n, wasteful otherwise.

sections.title: Lambdas
sections.body: `[&]` captures everything by reference (no copies); `[=]` by value. A recursive lambda needs `function<void(int)> dfs = [&](int u) { ... dfs(v); ... };` — capture by reference so it can see itself and your arrays.
